newsitem.title: UK: More overseas investors to get tax-free gilts - govt.
newsitem.headline: More overseas investors to get tax-free gilts - govt.

text.p: The British government said on Monday it will allow additional categories of overseas investors to receive interest payments on gilts with no tax deducted.
This will be of particular benefit to foreign pension schemes and foreign mutual investment funds, the Inland Revenue said.
It is intended that the the changes will be introduced next year, the Inland Revenue said.
Under the proposed new arrangements, those who can receive their gilt interest with no tax deducted will be extended to include -
-- foreign pension schemes eligible to participate in PFPVs
-- individuals who are not ordinarily resident in the UK
"I particularly welcome the deregulatory benefits which will be obtained under the new arrangements," said Angela Knight, economic secretary to the Treasury.
"I very much hope therefore that the consultations with interested parties can be completed quickly so that the necessary regulations can be introduced at an early date."

The new arrangements will operate on the basis of self-certification coupled with Inland Revenue audit and tax recovery powers. They will replace the three existing schemes, significantly simplifying the procedures, the Inland Revenue said.
The current schemes that will be replaced are the central gilts office gross scheme, the "E" arrangement and the central gilts office double taxation scheme.
The Star account scheme, introduced with the advent of the open gilt repo market at the start of the year, will not be changed.
